description: TerraSync is a team passionate about science, technology, and discovery. We aim to simplify complex scientific data and make it exciting and accessible, especially for young scientists and curious minds.
summary:
TerraSync is a web tool that turns NASA Earth data into clear answers anyone can understand. Users pick any region on Earth on an interactive map, choose a time period on a timeline (2001 to 2025), and instantly see how 16 NASA variables have changed there: air and ground temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, evaporation, clouds, wind, sunlight and more, from NASA POWER (MERRA-2).

For each variable, TerraSync removes the seasonal cycle, tests whether the trend is real with the Mann-Kendall test, and measures its rate with Sen's slope and a 95% interval. Instead of p-values, users read a plain verdict: "Clear change" or "Too early to tell", with a simple "then vs now" picture. A short quiz adapts the words and detail to each user, from a 12-year-old to a journalist, in English or French. Orbis, an AI assistant powered by Google Gemini, summarizes results and guides users to the trends, using only numbers TerraSync computed.

This directly answers the challenge: find variables, acquire regional data, visualize time series and test significance. It matters because climate claims are everywhere, but checking them has required expert skills. TerraSync turns rumours into evidence, for anyone, anywhere.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TerraSync helps anyone become an Earth data detective. After a 3-question quiz (role, age, language), the user sees one screen: a world map in the centre, a timeline below it, the region's NASA variables, and Orbis, an AI assistant, on the right. The user clicks or draws any region on Earth, picks the years, and gets a plain answer for each variable: "Clear change" or "Too early to tell", with how much it changed and a "then vs now" comparison. Two regions can be compared side by side.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Get NASA data: our Python server calls the NASA POWER API (built on NASA's MERRA-2) for 16 monthly variables from 2001 to 2025.

2. Cover the region: NASA answers one point at a time, so we query a grid of points inside the region and average them month by month.

3. Translate: each NASA code (e.g. T2M, PRECTOTCORR) becomes a plain name, a definition and a question; units become everyday ones (mm/day to mm/month, m/s to km/h).

4. Test: we remove the seasonal cycle (each month minus its usual value), test the trend with the Mann-Kendall test (Hamed-Rao correction for autocorrelation), and measure the rate with Sen's slope and a 95% confidence interval.

5. Answer: p below 0.05 becomes "Clear change"; otherwise "Too early to tell", which never means "no change".

Any region drawn on the map is analysed live in a few seconds. The timeline recomputes all variables for the chosen years, with a warning that short periods can mislead.

CREATIVITY

We turned a statistics test into a detective verdict anyone can read. The same data adapts to the reader: a 12-year-old reads "Water for plant roots", a journalist reads "GWETROOT, p = 0.16". Orbis (Google Gemini) can summarize a region or guide the user to its trends, but it never computes numbers: the server sends it only TerraSync's results and flags any number in its answer that is not in the data.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Free, global, no expertise needed, in English or French. Students learn how scientists separate a real change from luck on their own region; farmers check whether their area is really drying or heating before planning crops and irrigation; journalists fact-check climate claims in minutes; local officials compare regions to see where to act first. TerraSync turns rumours into evidence.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall), a Python HTTP server, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles, Chart.js, Google Gemini API, NASA POWER API.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Removing seasonal cycles before testing; correcting for autocorrelation; showing "too early to tell" honestly instead of hiding non-significant trends; warning that short periods can exaggerate trends; MERRA-2 resolution (about 50 km), so TerraSync studies regions, not single towns; a trend shows what changes, not why.

USE OF AI

The website code and the plain-language variable names were written with the help of Claude (Anthropic). Orbis uses Google's Gemini API. All numbers come from NASA data processed by our code, never from an AI.
